runs.text: The premise is not quite right: the authors did not strain the NiTi wires beyond the upper limit of their range. Their methods state the limit.

runs.quote: performed to avoid delamination of the coating from the wire surface.

runs.text: So that limit was set to protect the V2O5 coating. The upper strain level was also a deliberate choice for the main experiments:

runs.quote: and 10%, which would sufficiently exceed the saturation crack
density as reported for similar films deposited using ALD.

runs.text: In other words, the top strain was chosen so that the applied strain on NiTi would be well above the crack density that similar ALD-deposited films reach when saturated, so the coatings would be strained beyond their cracking threshold.

rendered: The premise is not quite right: the authors did not strain the NiTi wires beyond the upper limit of their range. Their methods state the limit. Tensile deformations beyond 10% were not[1] performed to avoid delamination of the coating from the wire surface.[2] So that limit was set to protect the V2O5 coating. The upper strain level was also a deliberate choice for the main experiments: We chose substrate strains of 5%[3] and 10%, which would sufficiently exceed the saturation crack[4] density as reported for similar films deposited using ALD.[5] In other words, the top strain was chosen so that the applied strain on NiTi would be well above the crack density that similar ALD-deposited films reach when saturated, so the coatings would be strained beyond their cracking threshold.
